grounds.reproductionOfTheTest: REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY. I implemented the restated rule from numberProduction's prose alone -- normalised mantissa 0.d1..dk x 10^E, scientific when E <= -4 or E > 16, positional otherwise, sign from the IEEE-754 sign bit, exponent as |E-1| zero-padded to at least two digits -- and compared it to the pinned primitive over 35 hand-chosen edge values and 599717 finite binary64 values drawn from 600000 uniformly random 64-bit patterns. instrumentAssessment.noVendoredEncoder: CONFIRMED. check-c2-v11.py contains its own ContractEncoder whose tags come from `spec["typeTags"]` -- the contract's registry -- and it imports no jx_canon. It does import check-c2-v4.py through a hash-pinned loader for node_census only, which is declared as 'the pinned node_census'. A precise caveat: the encoder both READS the contract's tags and, in obligations(), requires them to equal a hardcoded z/b/i/n/s/a/o. So the contract cannot actually redefine a tag -- it is read-and-pinned rather than purely contract-driven. That is defensible pinning, and it is checked rather than silent.

theThreeOfSevenBound.verdict: VERIFIED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS, and the declared split is exactly right.
theThreeOfSevenBound.byInstrumentation: I instrumented my own encoder to record which production branch fires while computing the head's skeleton digest. Exactly three fire: array, integer, string. Four never fire: boolean, null, number, object.
theThreeOfSevenBound.byPerturbation: Independently reproducing M17's logic, I perturbed each production's tag in turn and recomputed the head skeleton digest. It MOVED for exactly array, integer and string, and was UNCHANGED for exactly boolean, null, number and object.
theThreeOfSevenBound.theSelftestEscapeLesson: CONFIRMED, and the author's re-aiming was correct. The skeleton array contains ZERO object nodes -- its rows are two-element arrays of two strings, and the path token is itself a string -- so no mutation of object ORDERING can ever reach the skeleton digest. An ordering mutation aimed at that digest would have been a mutation that could not fail, which is the defect the selftest exists to prevent. Re-aiming it and adding M17 to execute the split was the right response, and M17 is a real test: I reproduced its exact partition without reading it.
theThreeOfSevenBound.tryingToBreakAnUnexercisedProduction: I could not break one THROUGH the skeleton digest -- by construction, since those four productions are unreachable from it. They are instead pinned by the vectors, and I confirmed the instrument reads the expected values for FF-5, FF-6 and all five FF-N vectors FROM THE CONTRACT rather than from literals: falsifying FF-N1's underThisText to n1:1 was caught by name as C2V11-VECTOR. So the unexercised productions are witnessed by contract-sourced vectors, which is the correct compensating control.

canIMakeTheCheckerPassOnAWrongArtifact.answer: YES. I constructed twelve artifacts that are wrong and that the checker accepts with exit 0 and FINDINGS: 0. The author's '17 mutations at 17 caught' is a true statement about the author's own mutation set; it is not a completeness claim, and more escapes do exist.
canIMakeTheCheckerPassOnAWrongArtifact.method: Each forged document was placed under a different filename so the subject-digest pin is skipped -- which the instrument declares in a SKIP line -- and every other gate ran.
acceptedWrongArtifacts: The central RULING reversed in prose: 'THE VECTOR IS RIGHT AND THE PRODUCTION WAS WRONG' changed to its exact opposite. ACCEPTED.
theSixLiveOnePointZeroLeaves falsified: one enumerated path replaced by a nonexistent path. ACCEPTED.
theSixLiveOnePointZeroLeaves falsified more plausibly: one entry replaced by a REAL path that holds 1.5, not 1.0. ACCEPTED.
All six entries of theSixLiveOnePointZeroLeaves replaced with fabricated paths, inside the operation payload. ACCEPTED.
selfVerification.twoIndependentEncoders.encoderBReproducedIt flipped from true to false. ACCEPTED.
numberProduction.howThisWasVerified changed from 'Mismatches: ZERO' to 'Mismatches: SEVENTEEN'. ACCEPTED.
selfVerification.measuredPredecessorDigests falsified: the recorded digest for c2-plan-stage-schema.v9.json replaced with sixty-four 1s. ACCEPTED.
numberProduction.positionalForm rewritten to state a DIFFERENT rule than the encoder implements ('always ends in .00, so 1.0 is written 1.00'). ACCEPTED.
numberProduction.scientificForm rewritten to deny that exponent form is ever used. ACCEPTED.
numberProduction.theRuling inverted inside the operation payload. ACCEPTED.
refusedAsControls: A closure member path falsified while the count stayed 17 -- caught by name, C2V11-CLOSURE-MEMBERS.
FF-N1's underThisText falsified to n1:1 -- caught, C2V11-VECTOR.
The published documentSkeleton.sha256 edited -- caught, C2V11-OWN-SKELETON.
The noOpInjections operation payload changed 193 -> 194 -- caught, C2V11-CENSUS.
Any narrative KEY renamed, or any list element removed -- caught structurally, C2V11-OWN-SKELETON plus C2V11-OWN-SUBTREE, because path or type moves.
numberProduction.sign prose stripped of 'sign bit' -- caught, C2V11-ENCODING-PROSE. This is the control proving the prose gate works where a phrase IS pinned.
canIMakeTheCheckerPassOnAWrongArtifact.theShapeOfTheGap: Every escape has the same shape: a STRING LEAF whose VALUE is false but whose PATH and TYPE are unchanged. The skeleton digest binds path and type only -- the candidate says so itself, twice -- so no prose falsehood can move it. The gates that do bind values bind a specific enumerated set: the vectors, the census counters, the closure count and members, the encoding's pinned phrases, and the derivation's own `from` restatements. Everything outside that set is asserted, not measured.
canIMakeTheCheckerPassOnAWrongArtifact.isThisBlocking: NO. companionInstrument.whatItDoes enumerates precisely the gates I verified, and claims no more. The instrument's own closing banner disclaims independent review. An instrument is not defective for failing to check what it never claimed to check. But the gap is real, it is larger than a reader of the green banner would assume, and three instances of it are worth naming individually -- see OBS-4, OBS-5 and OBS-6.

theSevenPointEightQuestion.question: How much of a green run is agreement between the artifact and an instrument built from the same reading?
theSevenPointEightQuestion.answer: Less than a green banner suggests, but materially more than zero -- and the split is unusually clean here, so it can be stated precisely rather than gestured at.
theSevenPointEightQuestion.whatIsNOTMerelySelfAgreement: Four properties are checked against something the author did not get to choose. (1) The head's documentSkeleton.sha256 and its 29 subtree digests are FIXED BYTES in a pinned predecessor; reproducing them from the contract's prose is a real external constraint, and my third encoder confirms the prose alone determines them. (2) The three predecessor digests are pinned bytes on disk; the derivation cannot be resolved against anything else. (3) Every `set` operation must restate type-exactly the value it replaces, so the delta cannot describe bytes that are not there. (4) The census, closure and skeleton counters are RECOMPUTED from the resolved contract, so they are measurements of the document rather than assertions about it. These would all fail if the artifact were wrong in the corresponding way, regardless of who wrote the checker.
theSevenPointEightQuestion.whatISMerelySelfAgreement: The reading of the prose. The instrument's encoder is a hand-written Python implementation plus ten pinned phrase assertions; it does not parse the contract's rules, it asserts that ten specific phrases still appear. Where a phrase is pinned the contract cannot drift from the encoder. Where it is not -- positionalForm and scientificForm, the two members that carry the actual substance of the repair under review -- the contract can state a rule flatly contradicting both the encoder and the block's own vectors, and the run stays green. I demonstrated this with a working control.
whatAGreenRunWouldNotCatch: Any false statement in a narrative string whose path and JSON type are unchanged -- including the artifact's central ruling, its self-assessments, and its account of how it verified itself.
A falsified enumeration that the instrument does not happen to re-derive, most importantly theSixLiveOnePointZeroLeaves -- the candidate's own headline correction.
A falsified self-report of a measurement, including measuredPredecessorDigests, chainDepth, leavesAdded, and the 600000-pattern mismatch count.
A contract rule stated in prose that contradicts what the encoder does, outside the ten pinned phrases.
Anything about whether the effective contract is a GOOD contract. Every gate is an internal-consistency or reproduction check; none is a judgement about fitness.
Anything about live corpus records. EPC-V2 runs over generated witnesses only, which the candidate states.
theSevenPointEightQuestion.theStructuralPoint: A companion instrument written by the artifact's own author converts an unverifiable attestation into a re-runnable check. It does not convert either into independent evidence. That framing is correct and I did not find a way around it. What this particular pairing does unusually well is make the boundary VISIBLE: the digest-reproduction gate reaches genuinely external bytes, and the instrument's declared scope is narrow enough to be audited. What made this review possible as an independent leg was not the instrument but the contract text -- because the prose was sufficient, I could write a third encoder and check the artifact against bytes neither the author nor the instrument controlled. That is exactly the property section 7.1 asks for, and it is the reason this candidate can be reviewed independently at all.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: It states that opensip-jx-canon-v1 'is TOTAL'. After this repair the number production is explicitly partial: numberProduction.rule opens 'Let v be a finite binary64 value', so NaN and the infinities have no stated payload, while the pinned primitive would emit n3:nan, n3:inf and n4:-inf for them.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItIsNotBlocking: The gap is unreachable in practice. check-c2-v9.py parses with parse_constant and converts every NaN/Infinity token into a named non-rfc-constant problem, so a non-finite float cannot reach jx_canon through the parse path. The encoding is total over everything RFC 8259 admits.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: One clause in the number production stating that non-finite binary64 values are refused by name, so the refusal lives in the encoding block rather than only in a predecessor checker's parse layer. This would also make the dataModel sentence 'A value outside these seven is refused by name rather than guessed at' literally true of the number production, which today it is not.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The 30-edge-value and ~600000-random-pattern test is reported without stating that non-finite bit patterns must be excluded. Drawing 600000 uniformly random 64-bit patterns yields roughly 283 non-finite values, which the stated rule does not cover; I skipped them and tested 599717.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItIsNotBlocking: The measurement is correct and I reproduced it at 0 mismatches. Only the description of the sample is imprecise.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: State the finite-only filter and the resulting count.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: It states that 'IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE section 7.1 repeats "across 5 live 1.0 leaves"'. That exact string is ABSENT from the current bytes of IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md under whitespace normalisation. I checked with whitespace collapsed precisely because a line-wrapped false 'absent' is the failure mode freeze section 7.7 names.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItIsNotBlocking: The citation was accurate when made and has been overtaken upstream. IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md was last modified at 17:13 on 2026-08-04, thirty-four minutes AFTER the subject was written at 16:39, and the freeze's current section 7.1 text now reads 'The affected-leaf count is 6, not the 5 recorded here first' -- the freeze itself attests that it previously recorded 5. The companion half of the same sentence, the attribution of 'five of them exactly 1.0' to IR-C2V10-NB-05, IS literally present in c2-plan-stage-schema.v10.review-independent.json, as is '8 float leaves' in the same sentence. So the substantive claim is fully corroborated and only the freeze pointer is stale.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Nothing in the artifact. Recording here that a successor should not re-verify that pointer against current freeze bytes and conclude the artifact misquoted.

nonBlockingObservations.severity: non-blocking, but the sharpest gap I found
nonBlockingObservations.finding: The candidate's HEADLINE correction -- that the affected-leaf count is six, enumerated by path -- is NOT re-derived by its own companion instrument. I replaced one enumerated path with a nonexistent path, then with a real path holding 1.5, then replaced all six with fabrications, and the instrument accepted all three with exit 0 and FINDINGS: 0. By contrast the exactly analogous closure enumeration IS re-derived, and falsifying one of its members is caught by name.
nonBlockingObservations.whyThisMatters: The candidate's own theClosureCount.whyABareCountIsTheDefect argues that 'A count with no member list cannot fail' and that 'Enumeration is what makes it a measurement'. The six-leaf list is enumerated but not measured by the instrument, so with respect to that instrument it is still an assertion. The principle is applied unevenly to the two enumerations, and it is applied less rigorously to the one the candidate leads with.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItIsNotBlocking: companionInstrument.whatItDoes does not claim to re-derive this list, and the underlying count is CORRECT -- I re-derived 6 by three independent methods and the enumerated paths are exact. The defect is in instrument coverage, not in the artifact's content.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Six lines in the instrument: walk the resolved effective contract, collect float leaves equal to 1.0, and compare the rendered path list to the published one. The instrument already computes everything this needs.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The candidate publishes a table of three predecessor digests it claims to have measured, and the instrument does not verify them, even though it independently resolves the same chain and holds all three true values in its own PINS table. I replaced the recorded v9 digest with sixty-four 1s and the run stayed green. selfVerification.chainDepth and the structuralDiff counters (leavesAdded, leavesRemoved, leavesChanged) are unverified in the same way.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItIsNotBlocking: The published values are all CORRECT -- I measured every one -- and the instrument verifies the digests it actually USES, refusing on mismatch. Only the artifact's self-report of them is unchecked.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Compare the published table against the chain the instrument already resolved. Two lines. The structural diff is similarly re-derivable: I reproduced leavesAdded 73, leavesRemoved 0 and leavesChanged 10 with the exact same ten paths.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The encoder is 'implemented from the contract text' in the sense that it asserts ten specific phrases still appear; it does not derive its behaviour from the prose. numberProduction.positionalForm and numberProduction.scientificForm -- the two members that carry the substance of the repair under review -- are NOT among the pinned phrases. I rewrote positionalForm to say 'The payload always ends in .00, so 1.0 is written 1.00', and separately rewrote scientificForm to say 'No exponent form is ever used'; both contradict the encoder AND the block's own FF-N vectors, and both ran green. The control confirms the mechanism works where a phrase IS pinned: stripping 'sign bit' from numberProduction.sign raised C2V11-ENCODING-PROSE.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItIsNotBlocking: The prose AS IT STANDS is sufficient -- that is the item-by-item finding of this review, established by a third encoder built from it. Nothing here undermines the reproduction claim. What is exposed is that nothing keeps the prose sufficient: a later edit could make the contract state a number rule contradicting its own vectors without the instrument noticing.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Add two entries to PROSE_OBLIGATIONS -- numberProduction.positionalForm pinning 'ALWAYS contains a full stop' and numberProduction.scientificForm pinning 'at least two digits' or 'mandatory sign'. The mechanism already exists and already works.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: This checker currently exits 1 with 4 findings, exactly as the task states: two PC-7-PINNED-ARTIFACT-IS-REJECTED (rust-provider-protocol.v2.json, threat-model.v3.json) and two PC-5-STALE-HEAD (c2-plan-stage-schema v9 vs v10, r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance v1.5 vs v1.6). Its observation list currently reads 'c2-plan-stage-schema: documents name v9, disk has v11 -- successor review state NONE; head correctly unchanged'.
nonBlockingObservations.consequenceOfThisReview: REPORTED, NOT ABSORBED INTO THE VERDICT. Because this review reaches a passing verdict on v11 with no blocking finding, that observation will correctly become a fifth finding, a third PC-5-STALE-HEAD naming v11 as a reviewed-passing successor that the documents do not name. That is the correct behaviour of that checker and the correct record of what has happened. It is a coordinator's decision whether to repoint the head; this lane closes no row and repoints nothing, and CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The claim that the encoder drives 'its tags from the contract's own registry' is true of the encoding path -- self.tags is spec['typeTags'] -- but obligations() additionally requires those tags to equal a hardcoded z/b/i/n/s/a/o mapping. The registry is therefore read AND pinned; the contract could not actually redefine a tag.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItIsNotBlocking: This is defensible and, more importantly, it is CHECKED rather than silent: a divergence produces a named finding. It is belt-and-braces, not a false claim. Recorded only so a reader does not over-read 'driven from the registry' as meaning the encoder would follow a re-tagged contract.

verifiedInputs.measurementDiscipline: Every digest below was measured this run with shasum -a 256 and compared character by character against the value declared in the task or in the artifact. None was taken on recollection.

ARCHITECTURE-TO-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md.readOnly: This file was never opened for writing by this lane.

derivationResolution.resolver: check-completeness.py derivation_declaration() and resolve_derivation(), imported and applied -- not reimplemented, not read as a document

checkersRun.headInstrumentStillGreen: check-c2-v9.py exits 0 over the head, unchanged, and its bytes were re-measured after all of this lane's work and are identical.

verifiedInputs.whatThisLaneWrote: Exactly one file: artifacts/c2-plan-stage-schema.v11.review-independent.json. No checker was edited, including the one under review. All forged documents built to attack the instrument were written under the session scratchpad and never inside the repository. Both subject digests and the head instrument's digest were re-measured after the attacks and are byte-identical to their values at the start of this review.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not re-verify the head. c2-plan-stage-schema.v9.json's own correctness is out of scope; I used it only as a source of pinned bytes against which to test the reproduction claim, and I confirmed its instrument still exits 0.

I did not re-adjudicate anything the v9 or v10 reviews settled, except where v11 reopens it. In particular the ALIAS ruling and its closed-envelope leg were not re-examined; v11 raises an objection against its own ruling there and I did not adjudicate that objection.

I did not verify MINIMALITY of documentIdentityEncoding. I established the text is SUFFICIENT to reproduce the head's digests; I did not test whether any sentence could be removed while remaining sufficient. The candidate makes the same disclaimer.

I did not execute EPC-V2 over any live ActivationManifestV1, EvaluationAuthoritySealV1 or TerminalRunV1 record. No such record was examined by me or by the instrument, and the freeze section 7.1 row remains undischarged.

I did not audit check-c2-v4.py, which the instrument imports through a hash-pinned loader for node_census. I verified the pin is enforced and that the recomputed census matches all nine published counters, but I did not independently reimplement node_census; the fixpoint experiment therefore inherits that primitive's definition of a no-op injection.

I did not exhaustively enumerate the escape set. I found twelve accepted wrong artifacts by targeted probing; I did not attempt to characterise the full space of prose falsehoods the instrument accepts, and I expect it to be large, since it is approximately 'every string leaf the instrument does not specifically re-derive'.

I did not test the instrument against a subject at a different derivation depth, against a malformed derivation declaration, or against a predecessor chain that revisits a file. The selftest covers digest mismatch and type-exact `from`, and I confirmed those, but I did not probe the resolver's cycle and depth guards myself.

I did not verify the remaining corpus checkers beyond exit status. I ran the seven required checkers plus check-package-coherence.py and read the latter's findings, but I did not audit what any of them measure.

I did not evaluate whether the effective contract is a good design. Every judgement in this review is about internal consistency, reproducibility and the accuracy of stated claims -- none is about fitness for purpose.

I did not verify the claim that the author's two encoders 'share no code with each other'. That is unobservable from the artifact; I substituted the stronger available test, which was to write a third encoder myself and confirm the published digests fall out of the contract text alone.
